area_title: Core SqlBulkCopy API / options / source data / type mapping / internal transaction road
what_area_is_about: why SqlBulkCopy exists as a direct SQL Server bulk-insert path instead of EF Core row-by-row SaveChanges
SqlBulkCopy constructors and lifecycle: destination table, WriteToServer overloads, Close/Dispose
supported source data shapes: DataTable, DataRow arrays, IDataReader, DbDataReader-style sources
ColumnMappings by source/destination names or ordinals, and behavior when mappings are partial or omitted
SqlBulkCopyOptions such as TableLock, KeepIdentity, KeepNulls, CheckConstraints, FireTriggers and internal transaction behavior
C# to SQL Server type compatibility, nullable/default value behavior, identity columns, and failure/error caveats
key_ideas: SqlBulkCopy is a fast load API; it bypasses EF change tracking and does not perform update/merge semantics by itself.
Source shape and destination table shape must be intentionally aligned; explicit column mappings are safer than relying on positional defaults.

Bulk options are operational switches, not magic safety: TableLock can improve throughput but affects concurrency; KeepIdentity/KeepNulls change inserted values; constraints/triggers may or may not run depending on flags.
Type conversion, nullability, defaults, identity values and constraint failures should be validated before the bulk call when possible.
Transactions can be caller-managed or internal; this area introduces the option, while staging/retry/failed-row isolation is left for the later R02/R03 pass.
Error behavior can be coarse: a bad mapping/type/row can fail the operation, so production-grade handling usually needs staging, validation or chunking.
